newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums drift in holiday lethargy.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums drift in holiday lethargy.

text.p: NWE gas oil cargo premiums were mainly unchanged on Monday, shrugging off stronger futures in lethargic physical trade slowed by a holiday in much of Europe, traders said.
The front month June IPE gas oil futures contract was $4.50 stronger at $177.50 a tonne at 1140 GMT, tracking Friday's gains in crude. July was $4.25 firmer at $178.75 a tonne.
"It's all on hold," a cargo trader said, reflecting the thin holiday-affected market in Europe apart from London and Geneva.
Low sulphur diesel was offered at a premium of about $10 over June IPE for end-month deliveries, but despite some active discussion no bids were forthcoming by midday.
"The product is available and the buying interest is there but people are holding back for now," a trader said.
German quality heating oil was bid at June +$3.50 and offered at June +$4.25. FOD was notionally assessed at June +3/$4.50.
The barge market was slumbering, with mainland European traders absent and the few participants at their desks discouraged by the stronger outright prices.
"We might not see any buying at all today because the prices are now so high," one barge trader said.
